Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title follows the conventional commit format type(scope): description. It is 45 characters, within the 50-character limit. It names the main change: the retired canvas model is replaced in the playground, which matches the diff that switches the default model in the route and the page.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description covers the Summary section with the problem and the approach. It explains the retired model, the deactivated provider mapping, and the new default. The Verification section lists the test command, the new spec, and the lint results. The Rollback section has the revert checkbox checked. The Database migration section is not needed because the PR adds no migration, so omitting it is acceptable. The Verification section could include more direct evidence, but it is concrete enough to decide on.
Full details: Rollback Plan

**Explanation** The PR description has a "## Rollback" section. It contains a checked item: "- [x] A plain revert of the squash commit is safe." This confirms that a plain revert is safe, which the check accepts. The section is not missing and does not contain only the template comment. The unchecked-style template clause ("Otherwise, the steps (flag or env var to flip, contract migration to run first)") remains in the text, but it does not change the confirmation. No code inspection was needed for this description-only criterion.
Full details: Verification Shown

**Explanation** The pull request description has a "## Verification" section that meets the check. It states the command that was run: `npx vitest run -c vite.config.mts apps/playground/src/app/api/canvas/generate/route.spec.ts`. It also states what the run showed: the new spec calls the route without a `model`, checks that the pinned provider mapping is not deactivated, fails with the old default, and passes with the new one. It adds that Prettier and eslint are clean on the changed files, and that no live provider request was sent. This is a concrete test command with reported results, not a bare "tested locally" or a CI-only claim. I did not re-run the test or inspect the spec file. The check judges the stated verification, not whether the claimed results are true.
